$comment: Registry of every place the ACDP maintenance-posture paragraph is copied.
The paragraph has ONE owner: the spec repo's README. Every other occurrence is a
verbatim copy, regenerated mechanically and never retyped. This file is what makes
'is every copy current?' a checkable question instead of a hope.
Adding a copy anywhere in the org means adding it here in the same change.
The paragraph is extracted by anchoring on its first and last sentence, AFTER
whitespace normalisation. Order matters: copies are hard-wrapped at different
widths, so the end anchor is split across a newline in some of them and anchoring
on raw text reports a false DRIFT. Normalise first, then anchor.
The start anchor deliberately includes 'ACDP is' -- 'a single maintainer' alone
also matches the website footer paraphrase and a spec CHANGELOG entry, neither of
anchors.start: ACDP is maintained by a single maintainer
anchors.end: Security reports: see SECURITY.md in the org profile.

canonical.note: Sole owner of the wording. Changes here are expected to propagate outward.

copies.note: Org profile front page. Keeps a '**Project status.**' run-in prefix instead of a heading and is hard-wrapped to 81 columns; both are local adaptations that survive normalisation. Wrapped at 81 columns with the prefix included in the wrap. Regenerate with posture/regenerate.py -- never retype. An HTML comment above the paragraph repeats the registration rule where a copy-paste would actually start.

Under a '## Project status' heading, hard-wrapped. Wrapped at 80 columns, starting at column 1 under the heading -- deliberately not our 81, confirmed by that session on 2026-09-06. Width is cosmetic because comparison is whitespace-normalised; recorded so nobody 'corrects' it toward ours. Went stale once (their #26, fixed 2026-09-06); that staleness is why this check exists.

unscannable.reason: Private. A GITHUB_TOKEN scoped to the .github repo cannot read it, so this check cannot cover it. Reported as uncovered on every run rather than skipped, so coverage is never overstated.
unscannable.known_state: components/footer.tsx:125 carries a one-line paraphrase with no version claims -- deliberately not a copy (see 'excluded').

excluded.reason: Paraphrase, not a copy: 'Maintained by a single maintainer on a best-effort basis, with no SLA.' Makes no version or RFC-status claim, so it cannot go stale the way a copy can. Verified 2026-09-05. Do not 'fix' this to match canonical.
Historical record of when the posture section was introduced, naming RFC-ACDP-0015 as Draft because it was Draft then. A changelog entry is supposed to stay wrong about the present. Never re-sync it.
